body.title: Run Claude and Codex on Ollama models

summary.prose: insrc can run its model work on the Claude Code and Codex command-line tools or on local Ollama models, but it cannot run those command-line tools on models that Ollama serves, including Ollama's hosted cloud models. This Epic lets a user pick, for any model tier, the Claude or Codex tool running on an Ollama model, from a list of models insrc declares as supported, marked cloud or local. The choice is offered the same way in the terminal UI, the VS Code extension and the JetBrains plugin, and the daemon runs it with the same structured, checked answers it gets today.

body.problem: Every tier of insrc's model work resolves to one of three runners: the Claude command-line tool on Anthropic's service, the Codex command-line tool on OpenAI's service, or a local Ollama model called directly [[c1]]. A user who wants the agentic behaviour of the Claude or Codex tool but on models served through Ollama, most often Ollama's hosted cloud models, has no way to ask for it: the families insrc knows, the approved-model records and the tier settings all admit only those three runners [[c2]] [[c3]], and the settings screens in the terminal UI and both IDE plugins offer nothing else [[c5]]. Such a user must leave insrc's settings and hand-edit tool configuration outside it, with no check that the model chosen can serve insrc's requests, no indication of which models are expected to work, and no record in insrc of what is actually running. The combination works in practice: both tools returned schema-conforming answers through Ollama in a probe, while a local model on a typical laptop was too slow for the Claude tool's prompt [[c6]], so users need guidance on which models to choose rather than an open field.

nonGoals.text: Changing how the daemon's embeddings or a local model share the GPU when both run at once.
nonGoals.rationale: User decision: GPU contention between a local Ollama model and the daemon's embeddings is out of scope for this Epic [[c4]].

nonGoals.text: Offering the new runners in the installers' default model setup.
nonGoals.rationale: User decision: the installers' defaults are out of scope; the runners are reached through settings only [[c4]].

nonGoals.text: Discovering and offering whatever models a user's Ollama happens to have installed.
nonGoals.rationale: User decision: the supported models for each new runner come from insrc's model definitions, not from what is installed [[c4]].

nonGoals.text: Calling Ollama's or any provider's API directly from insrc's own process for these runners.
nonGoals.rationale: Project principle: cloud model access goes through the locally installed Claude and Codex tools; direct REST providers must not be reintroduced [[c7]].

assumptions.text: Users of the new runners will mostly pick Ollama cloud models reached through a signed-in local Ollama, rather than local models.
Both command-line tools keep returning answers that match a requested schema when run on a supported Ollama model, as they did in the 2026-10-29 probe.
A local model on a typical development laptop may be too slow for the Claude tool's prompt, so local entries need to be chosen with care.
The model families, models, efforts and per-tier settings that already exist can carry the new runners without a separate settings scheme.

constraints.text: The models offered for each new runner are exactly those declared as supported in insrc's model definitions, each marked cloud or local; no surface offers a model the definitions do not declare.
Model work on the new runners reaches Ollama only through the locally installed Claude and Codex tools started as subprocesses; insrc's process makes no direct call to a model API.
The existing tier, model and effort settings are reused for the new runners; an effort is offered and applied only where the chosen model supports it.
The terminal UI, the VS Code extension and the JetBrains plugin offer the same runners and the same supported models, all taken from the daemon's one definitions answer.
Calls to a model provider stay serial, never issued concurrently.
Today's runners (the Claude tool, the Codex tool and plain Ollama) keep their current behaviour and settings unchanged.

requirements.statement: The runner and model choice can be made from the terminal UI, the VS Code extension and the JetBrains plugin, and each shows the setting the daemon actually uses.
requirements.rationale: Every settings surface must expose the new runners.

requirements.statement: When a chosen model or Ollama itself cannot serve the tier (for example Ollama not running, not signed in for a cloud model, or the model missing), the user is told why rather than getting a silent failure.
requirements.rationale: Users otherwise cannot tell a misconfiguration from a model failure.
